title: Root Canal Costs in Ontario and the Canadian Dental Care Plan
metaTitle: Root Canal Cost in Ontario and the CDCP Explained
metaDescription: How much does a root canal cost in Ontario? Cost depends on the tooth and complexity. Learn about the ODA fee guide and the Canadian Dental Care Plan basics.
secondaryKeywords: canadian dental care plan root canal
excerpt: Root canal cost in Ontario depends on the tooth and complexity. Here is how the ODA fee guide and the Canadian Dental Care Plan fit into the picture.
heroImageAlt: Dental treatment estimate with a tooth model, representing root canal costs and dental coverage in Ontario.
bodyHtml:
There is no single price for a root canal in Ontario, because the cost depends on which tooth is involved and how complex the treatment is — a front tooth with one canal is generally more straightforward than a molar with several. On top of the root canal itself, the tooth usually needs a permanent restoration such as a filling or crown, which is a separate cost. The Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) may help some eligible residents with the cost of dental care, and private insurance may also contribute. Below is how to think about cost without relying on a fixed number.

Why cost varies from tooth to tooth

Several factors influence what root canal treatment involves, and therefore its cost:

  • Which tooth it is. Front teeth typically have one canal; premolars often have one or two; molars can have three or more. More canals generally means more time and complexity.
  • Complexity. Curved or narrow canals, a previously treated tooth needing retreatment, or complicating factors can all affect the work required.
  • The restoration afterward. A root-treated tooth needs to be sealed and protected. A filling or a crown is a separate step with its own cost, and many back teeth need a crown.
  • Whether a referral is needed. Complex cases are sometimes referred, which can affect overall cost.

Because of this, the fairest way to understand the cost for your tooth is to have it examined and to ask for an estimate based on your specific situation.

The role of the ODA fee guide

Each year, the Ontario Dental Association publishes a suggested fee guide for dental procedures in the province. It is a reference that many dentists use as a starting point, and it is a reason fees for a given procedure tend to fall within a general range rather than being completely unpredictable. Individual practices set their own fees, so the guide is a frame of reference rather than a fixed price list. Asking your dental office to explain their estimate in relation to the current fee guide can help you understand what you are being quoted.

The Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP)

The Canadian Dental Care Plan is a federal program, administered through the Government of Canada, designed to help eligible Canadian residents with the cost of dental care who meet certain criteria, such as household income thresholds and not having access to other dental coverage. Where a person qualifies, the plan can contribute to the cost of a range of dental services, though coverage has conditions and may not cover the full amount of every treatment.

Eligibility rules, covered services, and the amounts the plan contributes are set by the federal government and can change over time, so the most reliable information comes directly from the official Government of Canada Canadian Dental Care Plan resources. If you think you may qualify, it is worth checking the current official details and confirming with your dental office how the plan would apply to a specific treatment.

Private insurance and payment questions

Many people also have workplace or private dental insurance, which may cover part of root canal treatment and the follow-up restoration, subject to the terms of the plan. If you have coverage, your plan documents or provider can tell you what applies. When you book, it is reasonable to ask the dental office how they handle estimates, insurance claims, and payment, so there are no surprises.

Does the CDCP cover root canals?

The plan is intended to help eligible residents with a range of dental services, but exactly what is covered and by how much depends on current federal rules and your eligibility. Check the official Government of Canada information for the latest details.

Why won't a dentist just quote one price online?

Because the right treatment — and its cost — depends on the tooth and its condition, a reliable estimate usually follows an examination rather than a generic figure.

Should I choose the cheapest option?

Cost matters, but so does the long-term outlook for the tooth. The least expensive step up front is not always the most economical over time. Discuss the trade-offs with your dentist.

Getting a clear estimate

The most dependable way to understand what root canal treatment will cost you is an assessment of the actual tooth, together with a conversation about fees, insurance, and any coverage you may qualify for. Dr. Neda Kadivar, a general and family dentist with over 20 years of experience, provides root canal treatment at Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham, Ontario, where you can ask for an estimate for your specific situation.

This article is general information and not a substitute for professional dental advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always speak with a licensed dentist about your specific situation.
